PAU 2027 · Selectividad

Inglés II: modelo 3

Texto sobre el sueño de los adolescentes. Hazlo en 90 minutos y después abre las soluciones.

← Inglés II en la PAUModelo 1Modelo 2Modelo 3Versión para imprimir

Instrucciones: Read the text and answer all the questions in English. Time: 90 minutes.

Why teenagers can't get up in the morning

Parents often complain that teenagers are lazy because they stay up late and find it impossible to get up for school. However, scientists say that the problem is biological, not a question of character. During adolescence, the body starts producing melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, about two hours later than in childhood. As a result, many teenagers are simply not tired at ten o'clock at night.

Since school still starts early, most adolescents sleep far less than the eight to ten hours that doctors recommend. Lack of sleep has been linked to poor concentration, bad moods, lower marks and even a higher risk of accidents. Screens make the situation worse, as the blue light from phones delays the production of melatonin even further.

Some schools in the United States have moved their starting time to 8.30 or later. In those schools, students sleep more, arrive on time more often and are less likely to fall asleep in class. Not everyone agrees, though: changing timetables affects parents' work, school buses and after-school activities.

  1. TRUE or FALSE? Justify. a) Scientists think teenagers sleep late because they are lazy. b) Phones can make it harder to fall asleep. c) Everybody supports later start times. (1,5 puntos)

    Ver solución y criterios
    a) FALSE: «scientists say that the problem is biological, not a question of character». b) TRUE: «the blue light from phones delays the production of melatonin even further». c) FALSE: «Not everyone agrees, though».

  2. Answer in your own words: a) What happens to melatonin during adolescence? b) What were the results of starting school later? (2 puntos)

    Ver solución y criterios
    a) The body releases it around two hours later than when we were children, so teenagers feel sleepy later at night. b) Pupils slept longer, were late less often and fell asleep less in lessons.

  3. Find words that mean: a) say that you are unhappy about something (par. 1); b) connected (par. 2); c) makes something happen later (par. 2); d) probable (par. 3). (1 punto)

    Ver solución y criterios
    a) complain; b) linked; c) delays; d) likely.

  4. Rewrite: a) Teenagers don't sleep enough. They feel tired. → If teenagers… b) Doctors recommend eight hours of sleep. → Eight hours… c) It's a pity I can't sleep more. → I wish… (1,5 puntos)

    Ver solución y criterios
    a) If teenagers slept enough, they wouldn't feel tired. b) Eight hours of sleep are recommended (by doctors). c) I wish I could sleep more.

  5. Writing (120-150 words): An email to your school's head teacher suggesting changes to improve students' wellbeing. (4 puntos)

    Ver solución y criterios
    Assessment: format and register (formal email: Dear Mr/Ms…, Yours sincerely), content, organisation and language. Suggestions could include a later start, longer breaks, fewer exams on the same day, quiet areas or sports activities, each with a reason.

Total: 10 puntos.
